fixture.name: same_fact_rephrased
fixture.why: One fact stated three different ways across the interview because the agent asks three overlapping questions.

expected_note: Owned it, was mine end to end, was the one driving it, and owning something completely are four wordings of one fact. Sole ownership is also consistent with others touching it and being secondary on call. Nothing here conflicts.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What were you responsible for in that role?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Tell me about the piece of the system you knew best.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The ingestion pipeline was mine end to end. I built the first version and I was the person people came to when it broke.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Nobody full time. Other people touched it, but I was the one driving that pipeline.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How did you handle being the only person who knew it?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Badly at first. Eventually I wrote the design up properly and ran two sessions on it so I was not the single point of failure.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Clickstream events, about two hundred million a day.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Tell me about a change you made to it that mattered.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I moved it from batch to streaming. Same pipeline, but the freshness went from six hours to under a minute.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Was anyone else on call for it?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I was primary. Two others were secondary, but in practice it came to me.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What did you like about that work?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Owning something completely. I knew every edge of that pipeline.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Being the bottleneck. Ownership and bottleneck turned out to be the same thing.
